title: Count Lattice Points Inside a Circle
summary: Given a list of circles defined by their centers and radii, count the number of grid points that fall within at least one of these circles, including those on the circle's boundary.
statement: Given a list of circles defined by their centers and radii, count the number of grid points that fall within at least one of these circles, including those on the circle's boundary.
constraints: Each circle is [center_x,center_y,radius] with integer values and positive radius.
A lattice point has integer coordinates and counts when its squared distance is at most radius squared.
Points covered by multiple circles count only once.
hints: Enumerate the integer bounding square of each circle.
Use squared distance to test inclusion without floating-point arithmetic, and insert accepted coordinates into a set.
For each x and y from center-radius through center+radius, add the point when dx²+dy²<=r².
The bounding square contains every possible covered lattice point, the inequality is exact, and the set deduplicates overlaps.
